arxiv-1812-03396.title: A Sequence of Cauchy Sequences Which Is Conjectured to Converge to the Imaginary Parts of the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
arxiv-1812-03396.creator: Stephen Crowley <stephencrowley214@gmail.com > December 8, 2018
arxiv-1812-03396.description: Abstract The convergence of a sequence of Cauchy sequences is conjectured; which if shown to be true, would prove the Riemann hypothesis by way of LeClair and França’s transcendental equation criteria. 1 Introduction LeClair and França established criteria for the Riemann hypothesis in [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2004-11049.title: On the Fourier analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon system: Growth and Decay of the Fourier constants
arxiv-2004-11049.creator: Athanasios Chatzikaleas
arxiv-2004-11049.description: Abstract . We consider the ( 1 + 3 ) (1+3) -dimensional Einstein equations with negative cosmological constant coupled to a spherically-symmetric, massless scalar field and study perturbations around the Anti-de Sitter spacetime. We derive the resonant systems, pick out vanishing secular terms and discuss issues related to small divisors.

arxiv-2106-03610.title: Modeling and characterizing stochastic neurons based on in vitro voltage-dependent spike probability functions
arxiv-2106-03610.creator: Vinicius Lima, Rodrigo F. O. Pena, Renan O. Shimoura, Nilton L. Kamiji, Cesar C. Ceballos, Fernando S. Borges, Guilherme S. V. Higa, Roberto de Pasquale, Antonio C. Roque
arxiv-2106-03610.description: Abstract Neurons in the nervous system are submitted to distinct sources of noise, such as ionic-channel and synaptic noise, which introduces variability in their responses to repeated presentations of identical stimuli. This motivates the use of stochastic models to describe neuronal behavior. In this work, we characterize an intrinsically stochastic neuron model based on a voltage-dependent spike probability function.

arxiv-2111-02529.title: Shift Happens: Adjusting Classifiers
arxiv-2111-02529.creator: Theodore James Thibault Heiser, Mari-Liis Allikivi, Meelis Kull
arxiv-2111-02529.description: Abstract Minimizing expected loss measured by a proper scoring rule, such as Brier score or log-loss (cross-entropy), is a common objective while training a probabilistic classifier. If the data have experienced dataset shift where the class distributions change post-training, then often the model’s performance will decrease, over-estimating the probabilities of some classes while under-estimating the others on average.

arxiv-2201-09995.title: Far and extreme UV radiation feedback in molecular clouds and its influence on the mass and size of star clusters 2020 Far and extreme UV radiation feedback in molecular clouds and its influence on the mass and size of star clusters – C

arxiv-2309-06065.title: Electronic structure and optoelectronic properties of halide double perovskites: Fundamental insights and design of a theoretical workflow
arxiv-2309-06065.creator: Mayank Gupta, Susmita Jana, B. R. K. Nanda
arxiv-2309-06065.description: Abstract Like single perovskites, halide double perovskites (HDP) have truly emerged as efficient optoelectronic materials since they display superior stability and are free of toxicity. However, challenges still exist due to either wide and indirect bandgaps or parity-forbidden transitions in many of them.

arxiv-2311-03278.title: Discretizing Numerical Attributes: An Analysis of Human Perceptions
arxiv-2311-03278.creator: Minakshi Kaushik, Rahul Sharma, Dirk Draheim
arxiv-2311-03278.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) has employed various discretization methods to partition numerical attributes into intervals. However, an effective discretization technique remains elusive in many ML applications, such as association rule mining. Moreover, the existing discretization techniques do not reflect best the impact of the independent numerical factor on the dependent numerical target factor.

arxiv-2401-00738.title: Bottom-hadron production in high-energy p ​ p pp and heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2401-00738.creator: \firstname Min \lastname He
arxiv-2401-00738.description: Abstract The hadro-chemistry of bottom quarks produced in hadronic collisions encodes valuable information on the mechanism of color-neutralization in these reactions. We first compute the chemistry of bottom-hadrons in high-energy p ​ p pp collisions employing statistical hadronization with a largely augmented set of states beyond the currently measured spectrum.

pmc-10518395.title: PD-1 blockade and radiotherapy combination for advanced Epstein-Barr virus-associated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a case report and literature review
pmc-10518395.creator: Chun-Xu Liao, Chang-Song Deng, Xia Liang, Jian-Chuan Yang, Zhi-Zhong Chen, Xiao-Ying Lin, Cai-Feng Lin, Shen Chen, Song-Song Wu
pmc-10518395.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is a rare malignant tumor of biliary epithelial cells, known for its extremely unfavorable prognosis. In the absence of intervention, patients typically survive for less than 5 months. Current guidelines from the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO), National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN), and European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) recommend chemotherapy-based systemic therapy as the standard treatment for advanced ICC.

pmc-10543838.title: Integrative evaluation and experimental validation of the immune-modulating potential of dysregulated extracellular matrix genes in high-grade serous ovarian cancer prognosis
pmc-10543838.creator: Qihui Wu, Xiaoyun He, Jiaxin Liu, Chunlin Ou, Yimin Li, Xiaodan Fu
pmc-10543838.description: BackgroundHigh-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is a challenging malignancy characterized by complex interactions between tumor cells and the surrounding microenvironment. Understanding the immune landscape of HGSOC, particularly the role of the extracellular matrix (ECM), is crucial for improving prognosis and guiding therapeutic interventions.

pmc-10562646.title: Nanoarchitectonics of photothermal materials to enhance the sensitivity of lateral flow assays
pmc-10562646.creator: Elangovan Sarathkumar, Rajasekharan S Anjana, Ramapurath S Jayasree, Katsuhiko Ariga
pmc-10562646.description: Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are currently the most widely used point-of-care testing technique with remarkable advantages such as simple operation, rapid analysis, portability, and low cost. Traditionally, gold nanoparticles are employed as tracer element in LFAs due to their strong localised surface plasmon resonance.

pmc-10753558.title: Calcined Bean Dregs-Hydrocalumite Composites as Efficient Adsorbents for the Removal of Ofloxacin
pmc-10753558.creator: Haohui Zhang, Xi Zhou, Deyi Luo
pmc-10753558.description: Calcined bean dregs-hydrocalumite composites were prepared through in situ self-assembly of hydrocalumite on the surface of bean dregs and used for the adsorption of ofloxacin from water. The adsorbents were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, X-ray powder diffraction, and N2 physical adsorption.

pmc-11419963.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Antiphospholipid Syndrome-Associated Venous Thromboembolism: Real World Evidence
pmc-11419963.creator: Hun-Gyu Hwang, Ju Hyun Lee, Sang-A Kim, Yang-Ki Kim, Myung-Shin Kim, Junshik Hong, Ho-Young Yhim, Soo-Mee Bang
pmc-11419963.description: BackgroundThe efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) versus warfarin in patients with antiphospholipid syndrome-associated venous thromboembolism (APS-VTE) remain uncertain. We aimed to evaluate efficacy and safety of DOACs in patients with APS-VTE.MethodsUsing the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database, we retrospectively identified all APS-VTE cases.

pmc-11437224.title: Effect of Semaglutide on Physical Function, Body Composition, and Biomarkers of Aging in Older Adults With Overweight and Insulin Resistance: Protocol for an Open-Labeled Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11437224.creator: Tiffany M Cortes, Libia Vasquez, Monica C Serra, Ronna Robbins, Allison Stepanenko, Kevin Brown, Hannah Barrus, Annalisa Campos, Sara E Espinoza, Nicolas Musi, Tiffany Leung
pmc-11437224.description: BackgroundOlder adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) or prediabetes are at increased risk of adverse changes in body composition, physical function, and aging-related biomarkers compared to those with normal glucose tolerance. Semaglutide is a glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist that has been approved for T2DM and chronic weight management.

pmc-11447267.title: Sex differences in DNA methylation variations according to ART conception-evidence from the Norwegian mother, father, and child cohort study
pmc-11447267.creator: Dana Kristjansson, Yunsung Lee, Christian M Page, Håkon Gjessing, Maria C Magnus, Astanand Jugessur, Robert Lyle, Siri E Håberg
pmc-11447267.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Previous studies have shown cord-blood DNA methylation differences in newborns conceived using assisted reproductive technologies (ART) compared to those conceived naturally. However, whether these ART-related DNA methylation differences vary with children’s sex is unknown. We hypothesize that the DNA methylation differences in cord blood between ART-conceived and naturally conceived newborns also varies by the sex of the child, with distinct patterns of differential methylation present in males and females.

pmc-11463786.title: Between land and sea: A multidisciplinary approach to understand the Early Occupation of Sicily (EOS)
pmc-11463786.creator: Ilaria Patania, Isaac Ogloblin Ramirez, Peyton Carroll, Kristen Wroth, Sara Zaia, Sebastiano Di Mauro, Danielle Falci, Iris Querenet Onfroy de Breville, Ignacio Aguilar Lazagabaster, Gianmarco Minniti, Agatino Reitano, Gianni Insacco, Tristram Kidder, Christian Tryon
pmc-11463786.description: The island of Sicily is considered to be among the first occupied by humans in the European Upper Paleolithic. Studies to understand early occupation of the island are mostly concentrated on the northern shores. Our project, Early Occupation of Sicily (EOS), focuses on southeastern Sicily so to address questions regarding dispersal to Mediterranean islands and Late Pleistocene landscapes and environments.

pmc-11470863.title: Comments on Global Symmetries and Anomalies of 5d SCFTs
pmc-11470863.creator: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Luigi Tizzano
pmc-11470863.description: We study various aspects of global symmetries in five-dimensional superconformal field theories. Whenever a supersymmetry-preserving relevant deformation is available, the infrared gauge theory description might exhibit a finite order mixed ’t Hooft anomaly between a 1-form symmetry and the instantonic symmetry. This anomaly constrains the flavor symmetry group acting faithfully on the SCFT and the consistency of certain RG flows.

pmc-12744400.title: Managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders in geriatric patients: past, present, and future
pmc-12744400.creator: Sarah Saxena, Yotam Weiss, Thomas Saller
pmc-12744400.description: Neurocognitive disorders remain one of the tricky perioperative complications, despite progress in screening tools and care bundles. BMC Anesthesiology has initiated a new collection on managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders in the geriatric patient, urging researchers to conduct large-scale, high-quality studies that address the existing knowledge and implementation gap.

pmc-13430182.title: Lesion-Level Association Between Artificial Intelligence–Derived Coronary Calcium Volume and Plaque Vulnerability
pmc-13430182.creator: Ruben GA van der Waerden, Joske L van der Zande, Jan-Quinten Mol, Pierandrea Cancian, Thijs J Luttikholt, Xiaojin Gu, Leah Heil, Tomasz Roleder, Jos Thannhauser, Simone Saitta, Clara I Sánchez, Bram van Ginneken, Ivana Išgum, Niels van Royen, Rick HJA Volleberg
pmc-13430182.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundExtensively calcified lesions are typically at low risk for lesion-level acute events, which may be related to less vulnerable plaques.ObjectivesThis study sought to evaluate the lesion-level association between total calcification volume and plaque vulnerability.MethodsData were derived from the prospective, observational PECTUS-obs study, in which patients with myocardial infarction underwent intracoronary optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging of all fractional flow reserve-negative nonculprit lesions.

pmc-13591841.title: Epigenetic clocks can differentiate between exogenous and endogenous skin ageing
pmc-13591841.creator: Christopher J Shore, Roy B Simons, Laura Ramos del Caño, Ziyi Xiong, Luba Milena Pardo, Christina M W Eecen, Tamar Nijsten, Kerrin S Small, Athina Vidaki, Manfred Kayser, Jordana T Bell, Y Jeremy Shen, David A Gunn
pmc-13591841.description: ContextWhereas factors originating internally to the body, such as blood nutrients and hormones, influence endogenous skin ageing, exogenous skin ageing results from the penetration of harmful factors through the skin’s outer stratum corneum layer.AimTo test whether an exogenous skin ageing epigenetic clock is more strongly associated with aspects of sun-exposure than two endogenous epigenetic clocks.

pmc-13627409.title: Clinical value of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and D-dimer in predicting the efficacy of minocycline for pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
pmc-13627409.creator: Rui Fang Chen, Xue Jiang, XinYing Zhou, QianYu Zhai, JunLi Wang, Shuo Feng
pmc-13627409.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) is a common respiratory infection in children. With the increasing prevalence of macrolide-resistant strains, minocycline has become a crucial alternative treatment. However, there is a lack of early predictive markers for evaluating early clinical response.
